proposed_from.topic: Quantitative weighted recession gluing for honest polyhedral-label inference. For a fully encoded finite-label Gaussian experiment on an unbounded rational-polyhedral fan, prove effective compatibility-density: every globally honest near-minimizer admits a finite core and recession library whose Gaussian-weighted path discrepancies, chart errors, tails, and weight-variation remainders vanish with a computable input-dependent modulus. Build CertGluePFL, a terminating outward-rounded primal-dual algorithm with complete rational geometry, covariance, loss-scale, accuracy, Gaussian-integration, and bit-cost receipts. Prove fixed-stratum, moving-offset, and compact-exhaustion multinomial transfer, and instantiate survivor-complier ordered-wage quantile labels for the Chen--Flores Job Corps setting under M_ASC>=m_*>0. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Fresh presolve derived kernel-independent Gaussian smoothing error s^2 sqrt(d/8), tangential averaging error ||a||_1/T, weighted path and exact coverage-repair inequalities, and an explicit compatible recession representation. Exact rational checks gave contact risk 14/15, preserved four-label r=4 and nine-label r=6 strict gains, and improved the rigorous eta=.05,r=2 enclosure to 0.361100<=M<=0.813799. Destructive checks covered seam-centered means, oscillatory rules, metric rescaling, covariance encoding, escaping dual mass, recursion, moving offsets, and target positivity without finding a model-level counterexample or literature collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove simultaneous ECD across the full recession incidence diagram with an input-computable refinement modulus and then derive global certificate convergence and complete termination recurrences. EARLY KILL TEST: On the exact four-label eta=.05,r=2 fan, emit an executable honest primal and finite atomic dual with outward-rounded gap<=.001 after charging every chart, seam, protected-neighborhood integral, tail, covariance error, and repair; the current width is .452699. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest geometric results are Burgos Gil and Sombra (2011, Theorem 3.4) and Kastner, Shaw, and Winz (2025, Theorems 3.32 and 4.8): they establish or compute compatible recession incidence, but contain no statistical kernel and no weighted approximation modulus. The closest computational result is Jones and Peet (2018, Corollary 4), which encloses one Gaussian-polytope probability after smoothing and truncation; the first changed step here is simultaneous nested averaging of an arbitrary honest rule over the entire incidence diagram before any finite program exists. The closest decision results are Goldenshluger, Juditsky, and Nemirovski (2015) and Schafer and Stark (2009), whose compact parameter sets exclude escaping primal constraints and dual mass. Carter (2002) transports bounded decisions only after a fixed positive-support experiment is specified; the proposal additionally derives one moving-offset rule and orders certificate approximation before compact exhaustion. For the causal consumer, Imai (2008) supplies truncation-by-death quantile bounds, Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2013, Section 5, Proposition 1, and Section 6.4) supply Job Corps always-employed survivor average and multiple-quantile bounds under assignment, Chen and Flores (2015) address always-employed complier means under noncompliance, and Dong and Heiler (2026, Assumption 3.2, Proposition 3.1, and Theorem 4.1) establish sharp mean SLATE bounds and inference for always-selected compliers under complier-conditional weak selection monotonicity. The present causal bridge instead targets a finite-grid quantile-effect semantic-label object, defines the full latent-law fiber for always-selected compliers under noncompliance and covariate-directional selection, obtains each fixed-quantile effect endpoint through a separate same-law optimization, retains only Cartesian-product containment for the joint vector, and builds simultaneous semantic labels with replayable minimax certification. None of these causal comparators contains the unbounded recession-compatible rule-density theorem or the moving-face Gaussian-to-multinomial certification kernel.

seed_details.destination_search: Searches for weighted recession gluing, effective polyhedral compactification, and Gaussian rule approximation found compatible fans and combinatorial Hasse diagrams but no rule-level modulus.
adjacent_threads: KastnerShawWinz2025: Theorems 3.32 and 4.8 compute the compactified face lattice after a compatible recession fan is available, without a weighted rule approximation.
JonesPeet2018GaussianDP: Theorem 2 and Corollary 4 control smoothing, truncation, and discretization for one Gaussian-polytope integral, not an incidence diagram of kernels.
CousinsVempala2018: Theorems 1.1--1.3 provide randomized relative-error Gaussian volume computation in an oracle model, not deterministic outward certificates.
seed_details.novelty_check: No located theorem couples a common recession subdivision to simultaneous Gaussian-weighted approximation of arbitrary globally honest action kernels with an input-computable vanishing modulus.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Burgos Gil and Sombra because their polygonal-strip proof already makes all recession cones compatible.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their finite cover has no statistical rule, Gaussian weight, approximation rate, protected seam, or computable refinement level, so it cannot imply uniform honest-risk approximation.
